name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
native: Российская Советская Федеративная Социалистическая Республика (Rossiyskaya Sovetskaya Federativnaya Sotsialisticheskaya Respublika)

predecessors.name: Russian Republic
predecessors.text: the Russian Republic of 1917; the infobox lists it (1918), the Russian State (1920), the Far Eastern Republic (1922) and the Priamurye Government (1923) as predecessors

predecessors.name: Russian State
predecessors.text: Omsk and Western Siberia, the Urals: retaken 1919

ledger.x: 1917, 7 November: the Russian Soviet Republic is proclaimed in Petrograd after the October Revolution; the Soviet republic is proclaimed again on 25 January 1918 by the Third All-Russian Congress of Soviets.
1918: the capital moves from Petrograd to Moscow.
1917 November to 1918 February: Soviet power is set up across Russia proper.
1918, 3 March: Brest-Litovsk: Soviet Russia "gave up claims to Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, most of Belarus, and Ukraine" and returned Kars, Ardahan and Batum to the Ottomans.
1918, 30 April: the Turkestan ASSR is formed inside the RSFSR; it is the RSFSR's autonomous republic until it is disbanded on 27 October 1924.
1918, June: the Czechoslovak Legion "captured Samara" in June, which enabled "the first anti-Bolshevik local government in Siberia, the Komuch, formed on 8 June".

1918, 13 June: "On 13 June, Whites formed the Provisional Siberian Government in Omsk" after White officers' organizations overthrew the Bolsheviks there (no date); the Legion "quickly occupied" Petropavl, Kurgan, Novonikolaevsk and Mariinsk and "took Tyumen" in July.
1918, July: the constitution gives the state its name, the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic (RSFSR); the page gives no day.
1918, July: White Russian troops under Kappel "took Syzran"; the Komuch's People's Army.
1918, July: "Radola Gajda took Irkutsk" with the Czechoslovak forces; the Legion also "quickly occupied" Nizhneudinsk and Kansk after Chelyabinsk.
1918, 3 August: Japanese, British, French and American troops "landed at Vladivostok".

1918, 23 September: the Ufa Act makes the Provisional All-Russian Government "the sole bearer of the supreme power in the whole space of the Russian state"; the Urals and Orenburg were already outside Soviet control and are counted…
1918, 3 and 8 October: the Directory forces abandon Syzran (3 October) and Samara (8 October) to the Red Army.
1918, 21-24 December: the White Siberian Army takes Kungur (21 December) and Perm (24 December).
1919, 8 January: South Russia is established by the White movement on the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus; the Soviet claim on this land ends.
1919, February-April: the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates pass to the RSFSR.
1919, 14 March: the White Western Army occupies Ufa; in April it takes Sarapul, Votkinsk, Izhevsk, Belebey, Birsk, Bugulma and Buguruslan.
1919, 26 April: "the Gomel Governorate is created" inside the RSFSR.
1919, May: the AFSR offensive "forced the front to retreat from" Kharkov, Belgorod, Balashov and Tsaritsyn.
1919, June: "In June 1919, after a fierce battle, Wrangel's troops stormed and captured the heavily fortified city" (Tsaritsyn, now Volgograd).
1919, 9 June: "The Red Army retook Ufa"; in July the Whites leave Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk (25 July), and the Urals pass to the Reds.
1919, summer: the Urals west of the Trans-Urals line (Perm, Kungur, the Udmurt towns, Orenburg approaches) pass to the Reds with the Siberian Army's retreat.

1919, September: the Southern Front gave up "Kiev, Odessa, Kursk, Voronezh, and Orel between August and October" and "through September and early October the front retreated to the north again"; the page gives no day for Kursk.
1919, 30 September: the Armed Forces of South Russia take Voronezh and Orel; Kharkov, Tsaritsyn, Kiev and Kursk had fallen earlier in 1919.
1919, 11 October to 18 November: the Red Southern Front retakes Orel, Kursk (Orel-Kursk operation) and Voronezh (13 October to 16 November); the pages give the operations' spans, not days.
1919, 14 November: "Omsk was evacuated on 14 November, and the Red Army took the city without any serious resistance"; the White Eastern Front collapses.
1919, November-December: the rest of Western Siberia (Tomsk, Novosibirsk), Altai and the Steppe is lost by the Russian State as "the Eastern Front collapsed; remnants retreated to Transbaikalia".
1919, 24 November to 12 December: the Red Southern Front takes Kharkov and Belgorod in the Kharkov operation.

1920, 7 January: "The pursuing Red 5th Army took Tomsk on 20 December 1919... and Krasnoyarsk on 7 January 1920"; Kappel's army "was forced to find a route around the communist uprising in Krasnoyarsk".

1920, 20 January: "On 20 January the government in Irkutsk surrendered power to a Bolshevik military committee" (the Political Centre had formed in late December 1919); the Red Army "did not enter Irkutsk until 7 March".
1920, 3-10 January: the Red Southern Front takes Taganrog, Novocherkassk, Rostov-on-Don and Tikhoretsk.

1920, January: the Southern Front "pushed the Armed Forces of South Russia back to the Black Sea and North Caucasus by early 1920" (Rostov-Novocherkassk operation, 3-10 January); the page does not date Tsaritsyn (Volgograd) or the rest of the Don.
1920, 26-27 March: the Volunteer Army is evacuated from Novorossiysk; on 18-20 April the Kuban Army surrenders to the Red Army and the Kuban and North Caucasus are Soviet.
1920, 26 August: the Kirghiz ASSR is formed inside the RSFSR (renamed Kazak ASSR on 19 April 1925); it is a union republic from 3 December 1936.

1920, 14 October: the Treaty of Tartu "was signed on 14 October 1920" (in force 31 December 1920) and "Finland additionally received Petsamo, with its ice-free harbour on the Arctic Ocean"; the page gives no date for the transfer itself.
1920, 7-17 November: the Reds break through at Perekop and take the Crimea; Wrangel evacuates 146,000 people, the last boats leaving on 16 November.
1922, 15 November: "Soviet Russia absorbed the Far Eastern Republic."
1922, 30 December: the RSFSR unites with the Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Transcaucasian republics to form the USSR; it stays a union republic with its borders and is the largest unit of the Union.

1923, June: "The remainder of the White Army were defeated near Okhotsk on 6 June and near Ayan on 16 June" and Pepelyayev "was captured after the battle of Ayan"; when the Soviet Union was formed on 30 December 1922 "the only Russian territory still controlled by the White…
1924, March: "Russia returns most of the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates and parts of Smolensk to the republic, doubling it to 110,600 km2."
1924, 14 October: the Kara-Kirghiz Autonomous Oblast is established "of the RSFSR" (a Kirghiz ASSR from 1 February 1926); it becomes a union republic on 5 December 1936.
1924, 27 October: the Turkestan ASSR, Khorezm SSR and Bukharan PSR are disbanded and replaced by the Turkmen and Uzbek SSRs.

1925: the Karakalpak Autonomous Oblast is "an autonomous area within the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic" until 1936; the Kazak ASSR page says the Kazak ASSR included "parts of Uzbekistan (the Karakalpak Autonomous Oblast)".
1926, 6 December: "parts of the RSFSR's Gomel Governorate, including Gomel and Rechytsa, are added" to the Byelorussian SSR, raising it to 126,300 km2.
1936, 5 December: "it became a separate constituent republic of the USSR".
1936, 3 December: the Kazakh ASSR becomes a full union republic; the Karakalpak ASSR passes to the Uzbek SSR under the 1936 Constitution.

1936, 5 December: "Accession of Karakalpakstan: 5 December 1936" to the Uzbek SSR; the Karakalpakstan page says it had been "an autonomous area within the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic" and became part of Uzbekistan "in 1936 as the Karakalpak ASSR" (it also gives 1932 in one passage).
1940, 31 March: the Karelian ASSR becomes the Karelo-Finnish SSR, a union republic.
1941, 16 July: "Their next target was Smolensk, which fell on 16 July" (the Eastern Front began on 22 June 1941 with Operation Barbarossa).
1941, October: Operation Typhoon takes "Oryol (captured 5 October)"; the page does not date Bryansk, Kursk or Belgorod, which fell in the same advance (October 1941 is an upper bound for them).

1941, autumn: the German and Romanian forces "took control of all of the peninsula by autumn" while Sevastopol "held out until 3 July 1942"; the Crimean offensive page says only that the Germans took control of the peninsula…
1942, 3 July: Sevastopol falls.

1942, summer (Case Blue, launched 28 June 1942): the Germans "recaptured Rostov, the 'gate to the Caucasus', on 23 July 1942", take Salsk on 31 July and Stavropol on 5 August, Maykop on 9 August, Krasnodar on 12 August, Elista on 13…
1942, 23 August: German troops reach the Volga at Stalingrad.

1942, 10 September: Novorossiysk "fell on 10 September, after a four-day battle"; "From August-September, the Taman Peninsula and a part of the Novorossiysk naval base were captured"; the Kuban bridgehead was held until 19 October 1943.
1943, 31 January: the Germans surrender at Stalingrad.
1943, January-February: "21 January 1943 - Red Army retakes Stavropol", "29 January - Maykop", "12 February - Krasnodar", "16 February - Rostov".
1943, 25 September: Soviet troops "completed the liberation of Smolensk" (and Roslavl the same day); "on 2 October the Smolensk operation was concluded" (Yelnya abandoned 30 August).
1943, October: Kursk was "retaken on 8 February 1943" and Orel "retaken by the Red Army on 5 August 1943"; the Bryansk Offensive Operation ran from 17 August to 3 October 1943.

1943, September-October: "16 September 1943 - Red Army occupies Novorossiysk" and "9 October 1943 - Red Army controls the whole of the Taman Peninsula"; the Case Blue page has the Kuban bridgehead held "until 19 October 1943", so the pages differ by ten days within October.
1944: "part of Abrene District, about 2% of Latvia's territory, was illegally ceded to the RSFSR" (the Pytalovsky district).

1944, 9-12 May: "An assault across the Perekop Isthmus was launched on 8 April"; Kerch was reached on 11 April; "the city [Sevastopol] fell on 9 May" and "the last Axis pockets in the Crimea were destroyed on 12 May".
1944, 9 May: Sevastopol is retaken.
1944, September: "the Karelian Isthmus with Vyborg (Viipuri) was transferred from the Karelo-Finnish SSR to the Leningrad Oblast".
1944, 11 October: "the Tuvan People's Republic was joined with the Russian SFSR" as an autonomous oblast (an ASSR from 1961).
1944, 15 October: "The Soviets captured Petsamo on 15 October" in the Petsamo-Kirkenes offensive (7-29 October), after the Soviet-Finnish armistice of 4 September 1944.

1945, January: "the Narva River was defined as the border between the Estonian SSR and Russian SFSR" and Ivangorod passed to the Leningrad Oblast; in 1945 Petseri County was ceded and became a district of Pskov Oblast (no month).

1945, 11 August to 1 September: the Red Army takes South Sakhalin (South Sakhalin Operation, 11-25 August) and the Kurils (Kuril Landing Operation, 18 August to 1 September); the Soviets were "entitled to annex" them under the Yalta agreement; the page gives no formal annexation date.

1946, 7 April: Kaliningrad Oblast (the former Konigsberg area of East Prussia, 15,125 km2) is "added as a semi-exclave to the Russian SFSR"; the Potsdam Agreement of August 1945 had placed Konigsberg under the Soviet Union "pending the final determination of territorial borders".
1954, 19 February: the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet transfers the Crimean Oblast from the RSFSR to the Ukrainian SSR.
1956, 16 July: the Karelo-Finnish SSR is "downgraded in status to that of an ASSR and re-subordinated to RSFSR".
1991, 25 December: the RSFSR is renamed the Russian Federation (Belovezh Accords signed 8 December and ratified 12 December 1991; the USSR dissolved 26 December).

wars.name: Russian Civil War
wars.outcome: Bolshevik victory: Ufa and the Urals June-July 1919, Omsk 14 November 1919, Rostov January 1920, the Kuban April 1920, the Crimea November 1920, Chita October 1920, Vladivostok 25 October 1922, Ayano-Maysky June 1923.

wars.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
wars.outcome: Signed 3 March 1918, annulled 13 November 1918; the claims to Finland, the Baltic lands, Belarus and Ukraine were renounced.

wars.name: Winter War
wars.outcome: The Moscow Peace Treaty of 12 March 1940 cedes the Karelian Isthmus with Viipuri, the Ladoga shore, Salla and the Rybachy peninsula.

wars.name: Soviet-Japanese War
wars.outcome: South Sakhalin (11-25 August 1945) and the Kurils (18 August to 1 September) taken.

wars.name: Eastern Front (World War II), German occupation of RSFSR land
wars.outcome: Germany invades on 22 June 1941, takes Smolensk (16 July) and Oryol (5 October 1941), the Crimea by autumn 1941 (Sevastopol 3 July 1942), and in Case Blue Rostov (23 July), Stavropol, Krasnodar and Novorossiysk (August-September 1942); the Red Army retakes…

certainty.note: Civil-war fronts, nominal Soviet control and the Far East; the Brest-Litovsk lands are claims.
Treaty and decree borders: the 1940 Moscow treaty, the 1944 Tuva, 1946 Kaliningrad and 1954 Crimea decisions.
